sections.h2: Who sends and collects property tax in Maury County?
sections.html:
The Trustee collects, the Assessor values, and the County Commission sets the rate. Both offices are on Public Square in Columbia and keep weekday hours from 8 a.m. to 4 p.m.

  • Trustee: Randy McNeece, One Public Square, Columbia, TN 38401, phone 931-375-2201. Checks go to Maury County Trustee at that address.
  • Assessor of Property: Bobby Daniels, 6 Public Square, Columbia, TN 38401, phone 931-375-4001.
  • Rate: set each year by the Maury County Commission.

The Trustee's page says tax notices go to the owner of record as of January 1 and that a change of mailing address should be reported to the Assessor. For a house inside Columbia, Spring Hill or Mount Pleasant, ask city hall whether a city tax bill applies as well.

sections.h2: What is Maury County like, and who is buying here?
sections.html:
Maury County is in Middle Tennessee, south of Nashville, and has been growing quickly. Columbia is the county seat, and Spring Hill, partly in Williamson County, is the largest city. The county was formed in 1807 from Williamson County and Native lands, covers 616 square miles, and borders Williamson, Marshall, Giles, Lawrence, Lewis and Hickman counties. Its farmland made it a leader in beef cattle production, and James K. Polk's home in Columbia is a state historic site.

Roads explain a lot of the growth. Interstate 65 runs through the eastern part of the county for about 18 miles, State Route 396 links it to Spring Hill, and US 31 runs through both Columbia and Spring Hill. The Natchez Trace Parkway and the Duck River complex add outdoor space. Maury County Public Schools operates the public schools countywide.

Census Bureau QuickFacts for Maury County show how fast the market has changed:

  • Population on July 1, 2025: 118,131, up 17.0% from April 2020
  • Housing units: 49,725, with 70.9% owner-occupied from 2020 to 2024
  • Median owner-occupied home value: $355,700
  • Median gross rent: $1,300, and median household income $76,130
  • Building permits in 2025: 1,408, and an average commute of 29.0 minutes

sections.h2: How does the 2026 reappraisal affect a Maury County tax bill?
sections.html:
Maury County reappraises every four years, and 2026 is the current reappraisal year. Values on the Assessor's records come from fair market value as of January 1 of the last reappraisal year, plus the equalized value of improvements added since. With prices climbing across the county, an owner whose house was last valued before the recent run-up should look at the new notice closely.

The formula is short. Multiply the appraised value by the assessment ratio for the property's class, then multiply that figure by the tax rate per $100. Tennessee assesses residential property at 25 percent of appraised value. A house appraised at $355,700, equal to the county's median owner-occupied value, would carry an assessed value of $88,925 before the rate is applied.

The county's 2025 to 2026 budget letter to the state Comptroller reports that the Commission passed a rate of $1.91 per $100 of assessed value with no increase for residents. A reappraisal year can lead to a different adopted rate, so ask the Trustee which rate is on your current bill. The Assessor's page explains the calculation and links to reappraisal guides.

sections.h2: When are Maury County taxes due, and what does a late payment cost?
sections.html:
The payment window opened on the first Monday of October and runs through the last day of February, so a Maury County owner can pay today, November 15, 2026, without penalty. The Trustee says all property taxes are due on receipt, and interest starts on March 1 at 1.5 percent a month, rising each month after that. On April 1, unpaid taxes go to Chancery Court.

The Trustee accepts partial payments, though interest applies to whatever is unpaid on March 1. A postmark counts as the payment date except when delinquent accounts move to Chancery Court. Tennessee law does not require the county to mail a notice, and a missing bill does not excuse penalty or interest.

  • In person at One Public Square, or through the drop box outside the office (no cash)
  • By mail to Maury County Trustee, One Public Square, Columbia, TN 38401
  • Online by credit card or e-check, with a 2.5% vendor fee
  • By phone at 1-877-556-4502
  • Monthly bank debits through the county's ACH program, set up by calling 931-375-2201

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Maury County reappraisal value?
sections.html:
Take it to the Assessor first, then to the local Board of Equalization, then to the State Board of Equalization. The Assessor's page confirms that a taxpayer who thinks the value is unfair can appeal to the local board and then the state board. Call 931-375-4001 to find out how and when the county board takes appeals this year.

The state's appeals guide sets the later steps. A disputed assessment generally must go to the county board first or it becomes final. A state appeal is due by August 1 of the tax year or within 45 days of the date the county board's notice was sent, whichever is later. For 2026 the August 1 date has passed, so an owner holding a late county notice should count the 45 days from the notice date. An administrative judge hears the case and rules within 90 days of the hearing, and a court petition must follow within 60 days after the state board's order is final.

Some assessors offer an informal review that may speed up a correction, though it is not an appeal and does not protect later rights. Ask whether the Maury office offers one, and file with the county board regardless if you want to keep the option open.

sections.h2: Is tax relief available to Maury County homeowners?
sections.html:
Yes. The Trustee's office helps elderly homeowners, disabled homeowners, disabled veterans and widows or widowers of disabled veterans apply for the Tennessee Tax Relief Program under state guidelines. Call 931-375-2201 for the forms and the current income limits.

The Trustee also offers ACH debits that can spread the bill into equal monthly payments. Call 931-375-2201 to ask how to enroll.

sections.h2: What happens to Maury County tax when I sell?
sections.html:
The tax year runs on the calendar, and the notice goes to whoever owned the house on January 1. A sale in the fall therefore leaves the seller's name on the bill even though the buyer will carry the house into the next year. Ask the Trustee for a payoff figure and have the title company divide the bill at closing.

A seller who is behind has less time than it seems. Interest begins March 1, and delinquent taxes are turned over to Chancery Court on April 1. A balance that comes due while a house is under contract usually gets paid from the sale proceeds at the table, so confirm the exact amount with the Trustee a week before closing.

faqs.q: Is 2026 a reappraisal year in Maury County?
faqs.a: Yes. The Assessor's page says reappraisals run every four years and that 2026 is the current reappraisal year. Values come from market prices as of January 1 of that year.

faqs.q: What rate did Maury County adopt?
faqs.a: The 2025 to 2026 budget letter reports a rate of $1.91 per $100 of assessed value. The Commission sets the rate, so check your current bill or call the Trustee to see the figure now in force.

faqs.q: When do Maury County taxes become late?
faqs.a: On March 1. Interest of 1.5 percent a month starts then and climbs each month, and on April 1 the county turns delinquent accounts over to Chancery Court. Payment is open from the first Monday in October through February.

faqs.q: Does Maury County accept partial payments?
faqs.a: Yes, the Trustee accepts them. Interest still applies on March 1 to any balance left unpaid, so a partial payment lowers the amount that accrues interest without ending it.

faqs.q: Who do I call to change my mailing address?
faqs.a: Call the Assessor at 931-375-4001. The Trustee's page says address changes go to that office, and it also says a bill that never arrives does not remove penalty or interest.
